article.opening: After moving through {{priorSign}} from {{priorSignEntryDate}} to {{priorSignExitDate}}, Mars enters Cancer on {{entryDate}}, and protecting what matters starts to outrank moving fast. We notice the strain in someone’s voice and step in. We wait until a choice feels safe before acting. Once we commit, we put deep emotional energy behind the choice.
article.tension: The trouble starts when protection moves faster than honesty. We feel hurt, decide something is unsafe, and act before admitting why. A simple question gets a defensive answer. We help without being asked, then treat the lack of thanks as proof that care is not returned. The anger moves sideways, so everyone reacts to the tone while the original hurt remains unnamed.
article.development: Mars last moved through Cancer from {{previousResidencyEntryDate}} to {{previousResidencyExitDate}}. The same pattern can return in small moments that seem unrelated. We handle what someone forgot and grow cold because the effort went unnoticed. We change the subject to hide how much something hurt, then hear the next harmless comment as another threat. Directness feels risky because naming the hurt would reveal how much it mattered. Indirect action feels safer, but it gives everyone the reaction and withholds the reason. Care then gets mixed with control: checking in becomes checking up, helping becomes taking over, and silence becomes a way to make displeasure felt. By then, the original need is buried under a conflict that cannot be solved clearly.
article.close: Before {{exitDate}}, the conflict keeps growing when everyone can see the defense and no one knows what it is defending.
try_this: We can take a brisk twenty-minute walk after a defensive reaction instead of carrying the heat into the next exchange.
We can ask whether help is wanted before taking over something someone else is handling.
We can name one hurt in a single plain sentence before it turns into a sharp answer about something else.
